_activity: Write it: outside evidence for Hamilton
_licence: ORIGINAL, built on the 11.2 casefile documents (numbered per the signed 11.2 map). Quotes are the casefile's adapted text.
source_document: Document 13 — Alexander Hamilton, The Federalist No. 15, 1787 (11.2 Casefile B)
source_text: Each state, listening to the persuasive voice of its own immediate interest, has withdrawn its support, until the frail and tottering building seems ready to fall upon our heads and crush us beneath its ruins.
prompt: Add one piece of outside evidence that supports Hamilton's argument. It has to be a fact that isn't in the document.
checklist: Is your fact outside the document?
Is it specific: a name, a date, a place?
Did you connect it to Hamilton's point?
model_response: Hamilton's argument is supported by Shays' Rebellion, when Massachusetts farmers shut down the courts in 1786–87 and Congress could not pay for an army to stop them. It shows the “frail and tottering building” he describes was not just a figure of speech.
